s: 1870 bakery famous for its spiral "escargot" pastries and long-fermented sourdough
w: A 19th-century bakery near Canal Saint-Martin, its painted glass ceiling and bevelled mirrors barely changed since 1870. The escargot -- a spiral pastry in rotating flavours like pistachio or apple-cinnamon -- is the draw, alongside long-fermented sourdough loaves with a serious crust. A reference point for traditional French baking.
_facts: Located at 34 Rue Yves Toudic, 75010 Paris
Known for spiral "escargot" viennoiserie in rotating flavours and long-fermented sourdough bread
Near Canal Saint-Martin in the 10th arrondissement

s: 1860 bakery with listed ceilings run by a Meilleur Ouvrier de France
w: A neighbourhood boulangerie-pâtisserie on the corner of Rue Tiron since 1860, its listed ceiling by Charles Anselme and carved woodwork evoking the Petit Trianon. Now run by Christian Vabret, a Meilleur Ouvrier de France, turning out bread and viennoiserie in one of the Marais's most ornate surviving interiors.
_facts: Located at 1 Rue Tiron, 75004 Paris, corner of Rue François Miron
Listed 18th-century decor including a ceiling by Charles Anselme
Run by Christian Vabret, Meilleur Ouvrier de France en boulangerie
